claims.text: The starting material is a composite of refractory high-entropy alloying elements and Cu.
A significant positive heat of mixing between the refractory elements and Cu creates a tendency toward phase segregation.
Machine-learning-optimized SPS parameters will minimize phase segregation in RHEA-Cu composites.
ML-optimized SPS will enable a large-scale reaction process.
ML-optimized SPS will produce a stable and homogeneous RHEA-Cu microstructure.
The resulting RHEA-Cu composite microstructure will be suitable for nuclear-reactor applications.
High heating rates and controlled pressure during SPS drive rapid reaction and densification.
Rapid heating and controlled pressure limit the time available for diffusion and adverse phase separation.
Optimized SPS causes rapid densification.
Optimized SPS limits grain growth.
Rapid densification and limited grain growth suppress the thermodynamic drive for phase segregation.
ML-optimized SPS accelerates reaction kinetics and densification.
Shortening the processing time kinetically inhibits elemental segregation despite the positive heat-of-mixing penalty.
The processed composite will have less phase segregation than conventionally processed composites.
The processed composite will have a finer and more uniform microstructure than conventionally processed composites.
The processed composite will have improved mechanical stability relative to conventionally processed composites.
Conventional slow sintering or reaction processing causes phase segregation and unstable microstructures through prolonged high-temperature exposure and diffusion.
The benefit of ML-optimized SPS is constrained by model accuracy and a narrow processing window, with segregation potentially recurring outside that window.
Existing evidence supports SPS as beneficial for rapid processing.
The magnitude of the improvement attributable to ML optimization for this RHEA-Cu composite remains unquantified.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator field says SPS suppresses the thermodynamic drive for segregation, whereas the mechanism field says the positive thermodynamic penalty remains and segregation is only kinetically inhibited. Rapid processing can inhibit realization of a thermodynamic drive, but it does not itself suppress that drive.
